№108954 "Website" should not be substituted into №108956 "Active on {0}"

Problem there, at least in Russian, adpositional (aka "second locative") case must be used here. This requires changing the form of "Website" from "Вебсайт" to "Вебсайт**e**", but

- Changing the form of the whole word "Website" might break other translations in the future.

- Idk what else platforms might substitute here, different preposition morphemes might be used (the use of "on" / "in" / "at" in Russian is complicated).

The correct string should be full sentence form, ex

- "Active on Website"

- "Active on Atari Console"

- "Active on Neuralink"

- "Active on Whatever Other Platform"

So, each sentence acts as own semantic unit and can be translated freely.

**And most important:**

I am asking once again to not step on same rake again and again:

Developers should not construct whole sentences using code unless it's tons of variations. 

And Crowdin should not be used as dictionary.

The substitution approach simply doesn't work with many synthetic languages (👉 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthetic_language ), because it requires changing the form of many words by adding specific morphemes (👉 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morpheme )  to make them semantically correct between each other.

The "{0}" substitution approach only works well if it's user content (titles, inputs, descriptions) and it's guaranteed to be nominative case (and Im still not sure anyway)
